Eine kleine Frage. Ein großes Problem. Z: One small question. One enormous problem. Two ways of looking at the same thing.
Die Aussage bleibt, nur die Erklärung ve: The central claim remains the same; only the explanation changes.

Warum wollen wir recht haben?: Why do we want to be right?
Stell dir vor, du siehst hinter dem Fens: Imagine seeing a cat beyond the window. Your friend says, “That isn't a cat; it's a shadow.” Who is right? Perhaps one of you. Perhaps neither. Only by looking more closely do you learn what is actually outside.
Eine Überzeugung ist nicht dadurch wahr,: A belief is not made true by how convincing it feels. We must distinguish the psychological state of holding something to be true from the truth claim of a statement. The correspondence view—that true statements accurately describe facts—is an important philosophical starting point, but neither the only theory of truth nor a complete method of verification.
Warum reicht ein Gefühl nicht immer?: Why isn't a feeling always enough?
Wenn du Angst im Dunkeln hast, ist diese: If you are afraid in the dark, that fear is real. But it doesn't follow that a monster is hiding there. Your feeling tells us something true about your experience. It doesn't answer every question about the world.
Erste-Person-Erfahrungen sind relevante: First-person experiences provide relevant information about subjective life. But anyone claiming an external cause needs further reasons. Distinguishing experience from explanation avoids two errors: dismissing subjective life altogether, and inferring an objective cause directly from the intensity or significance of an experience.
Vielleicht entdeckt ihr eine Taschenlamp: Maybe you find a flashlight. Suddenly you see: it wasn't a cat or a monster but a jacket. Is that embarrassing? Perhaps a little. But now you can pick up the jacket. You've learned something. That's the point.
Fallibilismus bezeichnet die Haltung, da: Fallibilism holds that our beliefs can in principle be mistaken. It does not mean that all opinions are equally good or that certainty is impossible in every sense. Rather, many claims become more reliable as they withstand criticism, alternative explanations, and fresh observations. Revision can therefore represent epistemic progress, not disloyalty.
Was hat das mit einem guten Leben zu tun: What does any of this have to do with living well?
Wenn du zugeben kannst, dass du dich gei: If you can admit you were wrong, you don't always have to win. You can stay curious. And your friend can disagree without becoming your enemy.
Aus Tatsachen allein folgt keine vollstä: Facts alone do not yield a complete ethical system. Moving from what is to what ought to be requires additional normative premises. We therefore explicitly propose an ethical stance rather than presenting it as a scientifically proven conclusion: the pursuit of truth should remain connected to human dignity, freedom, and a willingness to revise one's own views.
Not every feeling is an explanation.
Aber jedes ehrliche Fragen ist ein Anfan: But every sincere question is a beginning.
